source.title: Do Flatter Minima Drive Better Generalization? An Algorithmic Separation in Grokking

page_placements.theme: Flatness associations and their causal limits

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether flatness selects generalizing solutions and reports counterexamples, while refining the account to make weight decay select generalizing solutions and SAM accelerate escape in some settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports new modular-arithmetic grokking results, SAM+weight-decay transition speedups, theoretical comparisons of memorizing and generalizing interpolants, and figure-only results on image and language tasks. It also reports curvature metrics, but those measurements are not separately catalogued here unless they directly bear on a listed claim version. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study runs modular-addition grokking in 1- and 2-layer Transformers with regularization ablations (none, WD, SAM-only, SAM+WD; 5 seeds). These show generalization appears only with weight decay. That bears on V5's weight-decay/low-norm account, backed by a toy-model theorem that the generalizing solution has lower norm above a training-size threshold. It also bears on V1's scope, since grokking was absent without WD. Its main target is the flatness-as-selector hypothesis (Han et al.), which no listed version names. The image and language experiments report only SAM speedups, not the delay itself.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude flatness is neither necessary nor sufficient for the grokking transition: SAM-only gives the flattest solutions, which stay memorizing. Weight decay (lower norm) selects the generalizing solution. SAM accelerates escape from memorization, at epoch level, once WD has reached a low-norm regime. They report the same acceleration trend on vision and language tasks, but do not isolate the causal mechanism there.
record.recipe_differences: Adapts modular-addition grokking experiments using full-batch AdamW and compares no regularization, weight decay, SAM, and SAM+weight decay across SAM radii; also recreates image and language grokking setups. The paper describes the modular setup as an adaptation of prior work.
record.method_sensitivity: SAM radius affects transition speed: acceleration generally rises with rho up to a threshold, then can decline as SAM's first-order approximation becomes inaccurate. The modular results also vary by architecture and task; one 2-layer, mod-97 SAM+WD setting reports 0.903x.

fits_no_version.finding: Pairing SAM with weight decay shortens epochs to the grokking transition: up to 3.99x (1-layer, mod 97, rho=1.0). The gain generally rises with rho, then declines; one cell is slower, 0.903x (2-layer, mod 97, rho=0.05). A similar trend appears in figure-only CIFAR-10, SST-5, MNIST and IMDb setups.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A flatness bias (SAM) accelerates, but does not induce, the grokking transition once weight decay is present.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM-only runs reach the lowest Hessian lambda_max yet never generalize (0/180 pooled runs). In theory, memorizing and generalizing interpolants share identical trace flatness, and SAM destabilizes memorizing interpolants only in a low-norm window.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Flatness is neither sufficient nor a selector for grokking (counter to Han et al. 2025).

record.problems: The modular experiments use 5 seeds; practical-task experiments use 3 seeds. The smaller-training-set relationship and full training/test accuracy trajectory are not tested. Practical-task speedups are shown in figures without exact values in the text. The epoch-level speedup does not account for SAM's extra computational cost; the authors note each SAM update requires an additional forward-backward pass.
record.rows_left_out: Other SAM+WD rho-specific speedup entries are not individually extracted from Tables 2–3 to stay concise; the selected entries preserve examples across all four task/architecture panels and include the reported reversal. Curvature metric values are not included because they do not directly measure a listed claim version.

untested.parts: The delay itself: training-accuracy saturation timing relative to the test jump is not reported in numbers. Dependence on training-set size is not tested (fixed 30% split).
All: no circuit analysis, no progress measures, no tracking of memorization removal.
Existence of delayed generalization on image and text data is not measured (only SAM speedups, figure-only). The initialization-scale or weight-norm switch (lazy-to-rich transition) is not tested.
All in practice: no LLM pretraining. For SST-5 fine-tuning of TinyBERT and DistilGPT2, the delay is not reported, only the speedup.
Empirical critical dataset size and ungrokking below it; norm trajectories in trained networks.
All: optimizer is fixed (full-batch AdamW); no floating-point or softmax controls.

missing.what: Grok epochs under WD (e.g. 11169±4740 for 1-layer mod 97; 11266±9705 for 2-layer mod 113; 6770±1526 for 2-layer mod 97). These are the only timing data for the grokking transition.
missing.locator: Appendix A.4, Tables 2–3, Grok epoch column

missing.what: SAM+WD at rho=0.01 groks in only 4/5 seeds for the 2-layer mod 113 panel.
Pooled incidence: weight-decay methods generalize in 99% of 200 runs; no-reg 0/20; SAM-only 0/180.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 'supports' label relied on incidence and SAM-speedup rows that do not measure the delay, so it is dropped. The V3 and V4 'supports' labels relied on figure-only SAM speedups in recreated setups, where the delay itself is not reported, so they are dropped. SAM speedup rows are moved to fits_no_version. Epoch-level speedups ignore SAM's extra forward-backward pass. The authors scope their norm claim to full-batch AdamW/SAM and note the norm threshold may be optimizer-dependent (a cited result). The table text is partly garbled for Table 2(a) WD grok epoch and val acc.

versions.untested_parts: The training-set-size effect is not tested: modular tasks use a fixed 30% training split. The experiments do not report the full training-accuracy and test-accuracy trajectory needed to verify chance-level test accuracy after training accuracy saturates.
The study does not track gradual formation of a Fourier/generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or progress measures anticipating a test-accuracy jump.
The study reports grokking-like transitions on image and language tasks, but does not test switching the effect through initialization scale or directly test a lazy-to-rich transition.
The study fine-tunes language models on SST-5; it does not test LLM pretraining.

It does not sweep dataset size to identify a critical size or test ungrokking below such a threshold. The norm comparison is theoretical; empirical norm trajectories are not reported as evidence for the efficiency account.
The study does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax limits as causes of the delay, nor whether controlling them removes grokking.
